name: Persian
risks: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is an inherited disorder most often seen in Persians.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is more prevalent in this breed than in some others.

name: Maine Coon
risks: HCM risk is increased. A gene variant linked to this breed can be tested. Ask your vet about genetic testing and heart screening; a negative genetic test does not rule out HCM.

name: Ragdoll
risks: HCM risk is increased. A gene variant linked to this breed can be tested. Ask your vet about genetic testing and heart screening; a negative genetic test does not rule out HCM.

name: Siamese / Oriental
risks: Renal amyloidosis occurs more often in Oriental breeds. The source does not establish the same risk for every breed grouped under this profile option.

name: Bengal
risks: HCM is more prevalent in this breed. Ask your vet about suitable heart screening.

name: British Shorthair
risks: HCM is more prevalent in this breed.
PKD is occasionally reported in British Shorthairs.

name: Burmese
risks: Diabetes risk is higher in Australian and European Burmese populations. The same increase was not reported for North American Burmese in the cited study.

name: Abyssinian
risks: Renal amyloidosis is rare but has a breed association with Abyssinians. Ask your vet about the significance for this cat.

name: Sphynx
risks: HCM is more prevalent in this breed. Ask your vet to examine the cat and plan heart screening.
